title_original: Black Trauma and the Scars of Childhood
excerpt_original: Using the belt as a medium, Lex Marie interrogates the connection between intergenerational trauma and parental corporal punishment.

blocks.text: The most unreasonable expression I heard as a child is now the title of Lex Marie’s solo exhibition at The Bishop Gallery. “Because I Said So,” a quote that silenced many discussions and caused a mountain of confusion for children around the world, is transformed into a site that intends to unpack the entanglement of corporal punishment and care within Black households.
Marie presents 21 works. The dominant material? Belts. In this context, their practical purpose is stripped away, and they become an emotionally charged object used to investigate cultural practices.
